source.artboard: Chart --- Stat tiles and Chart card
source.how: get_computed_styles for the declared values; get_node_info / get_children for the laid-out rects, whose world coordinates are what `gaps` is computed from.

note: One figure: the first tile of the sheet's row — label, figure and change line stacked in a text column, the sparkline at the end aligned to its foot. The sheet nests the three text parts in a column frame; the code places them as <dt>/<dd> cells of a two-column grid with the trend spanning all three rows, because a <dl> may not wrap its term and descriptions in an extra element per pair beyond the one <div>. The union of the parts is the same box either way, and that union is what the laws read. Measured on the FIRST tile, which carries no start hairline; one tile only, because `measure` takes every matching slot on screen.

lawsNotDeclared.concentric-radius: A tile has no corner of its own: the row's frame carries radius-md and clips nothing, and the tiles are separated by hairlines, not shaped.
lawsNotDeclared.track-is-the-sum-of-its-parts: The trend is pushed to the tile's end (space-between on the sheet, a minmax(0,1fr) text column in code), so the slack between the text and the sparkline is free space, not a part — the track is wider than its parts by design.
